cells.gaps: No national figure for clinics entering their own reports: LBR-037 finds none in 48 facilities of three counties (2022), which does not carry the country, and LBR-043 and LBR-046 publish none. Nothing on where data is keyed is dated after 2022-07; the only last-twelve-months row (LBR-008) is dated to the year 2025 and cannot be placed inside the window, and the CBIS is described as a DHIS2 sub-system while its integration with DHIS2 is still planned, so no community flag is set.
cells.note: All facilities report monthly into the national DHIS2, keyed by district and county data clerks from the facilities' paper forms, which is the whole of rung 3. Rung 4 needs entry at the facility by more than half of primary clinics, and every source that speaks to it puts the keying at district or county.

cells.gaps: The number of Liberian facilities live is not established: seven clinics and health centers are counted across Liberia and Ghana together with no split or denominator, on the company's own account. Owners disagree by system: the running platform is vendor-owned (LBR-005), the planned national EMR is the ministry's (LBR-007) and the two-health-center EMR is UNFPA's and only commissioned (LBR-024, LBR-026); whether the 2020 hospital OpenMRS (LBR-031) still runs is not on record, and the 20% of public facilities for 2026 is a target.
cells.note: A handful of pilot clinics and health centers record at the point of care on a vendor's platform, which is rung 2. Rung 3 needs most T1 and T2 hospitals or primary clinics across some districts, and the evidence shows only named pilot sites and plans.
